SAS BRSHIFT(argument-1, argument-2)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_brshift.Rd

Bitwise right shift. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

a

Numeric value treated as an unsigned 32-bit integer (0 to 4294967295); non-integers and values outside that range are invalid. Missing gives missing.

n

Number of bit positions to shift right, an integer from 0 to 31; zeros are shifted in from the left.

.at

Internal: source position c(line, column) used in log NOTEs.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Implements the SAS DATA step semantics (log NOTEs, _ERROR_), which base R has no counterpart for.

See also

Other special functions: sas_f_band(), sas_f_blshift(), sas_f_bnot(), sas_f_bor(), sas_f_bxor(), sas_f_exist(), sas_f_input(), sas_f_inputc(), sas_f_inputn(), sas_f_missing(), sas_f_nvalid(), sas_f_prxchange(), sas_f_prxmatch(), sas_f_prxparse(), sas_f_put(), sas_f_putc(), sas_f_putn()

Examples

# BRSHIFT: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# Shifting 16 right by 2 bits divides it by 4, giving 4.
sas_f_brshift(16, 2)  # brshift(16, 2) = 4
#> [1] 4

# Shifting 255 right by 4 bits drops the low four bits, giving 15.
sas_f_brshift(255, 4)  # brshift(255, 4) = 15
#> [1] 15

# A missing argument gives a missing result.
sas_f_brshift(NA_real_, 1)  # brshift(., 1) = .
#> Warning: NOTE: Mathematical operations could not be performed. The result of the operation has been set to a missing value.
#> [1] NA
